title: refactor: remove obsolete Gen and registry plumbing
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Reconstructs the useful part of the stale branch on current main; keeps schema types and logging that now have real callers.
- Removes the unused Portkey multi-target request path and success-header reconstruction; the Worker fallback loop remains the sole retry owner.
- Rejects empty generic and Azure response streams as retryable 502s instead of fabricating successful SSE output.
- Removes unused internal exports and duplicate registry billing entry points: 132 fewer production lines, 264 fewer lines overall.

Validation:
- Biome and Gen typecheck
- 109 focused fallback, text-client, tracking, and observability tests
- Full Gen run: 104 files / 1,248 tests passed; the remaining community file passed 80/80 after supplying its Enter-only Stripe test dependency

gist.headline: One retry loop to rule them
gist.blurb: The Gen worker swept out some retired fallback plumbing and kept one clear path through the garden. Empty provider streams now get a proper retry instead of being dressed up as successful output.
gist.summary: Removed the unused Portkey multi-target fallback and duplicate registry billing paths, while treating empty generic OpenAI and Azure response streams as retryable 502 errors handled by the Worker fallback loop.
gist.impact: Text requests now have a single retry owner, so empty upstream streams are retried cleanly rather than returning fabricated successful SSE responses.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden-shed server room where Polli tidies away tangled, obsolete routing pipes while one sturdy lime-green watering channel carries response droplets to a retro terminal. The monitor robot watches a small empty stream jar get redirected into a clearly marked retry loop; code-plants and flowers show that the simplified path keeps the system healthy.
